title: Training Data
about: See how one word or one bad example can tip a model's choice.

cards.prompt: In this spam filter's examples, **"free"** only appeared in spam. Will it call **"Free pizza at footy training"** spam?

options.text: Yes: in its examples, "free" only ever meant spam
No: it can tell the message comes from a friend
options.nudge: It only sees the words. What did its examples teach it about "free"?

options.text: No: it knows people say "free pizza" all the time
options.nudge: It only knows its examples. Did any of them use "free" in a friendly way?

options.text: It can't guess: it has never seen this exact message
options.nudge: Guessing about new things is a model's job. What pattern does "free" follow?

cards.hint: Look at which kind of message "free" turned up in.
cards.explanation: To this filter, **"free" means spam**: that's all its examples showed. Friends say "free" too, but a model can't learn from examples it never saw.

cards.prompt: Teach the spam filter: tap **Spam** or **Not spam** for each message.

examples.text: Your parcel is held, pay the fee here
examples.label: spam

examples.text: Can you send me the homework
examples.label: ok

tests.text: Click to claim a free prize

cards.hint: Spam tries to make you win, claim, click or pay; normal messages are everyday plans.
cards.nudge: Ask of each message: is it trying to make you claim, click or pay?
cards.explanation: Your labels were right. The model caught the prize message, but called **"Free pizza at footy training"** spam: in its examples, "free" only appeared in spam.

cards.title: Words that vote
cards.body:
In this model, words **vote**. Each word of 3 or more letters gets one vote per training message it was in, for that message's label.

"Free" was in three spam messages: 3 votes for spam. "Pizza" and "training" gave not spam just 2. Most votes wins; a tie means "not sure".

examples.text: Your parcel is held, pay the fee here
examples.label: spam

examples.text: Can you send me the homework
examples.label: ok

tests.text: Click to claim a free prize

cards.hint: Which message shows friends use "free" too?
cards.nudge: Which message shows friends use "free" in normal plans? That is what the filter is missing.
cards.explanation: **"Free footy training on Saturday"** shows friends say "free" too, so the pizza message gets more not-spam votes. "Pizza, pizza, pizza!" adds one vote: a word counts once per message.

cards.prompt: Good data has **checked labels**, **variety** and **realistic** examples. Does each one make data **better** or cause a **problem**?

items.label: Labels checked by a second person

cards.hint: Ask: does it teach the model something new and true?
cards.nudge: Look for ones that teach something wrong, repeat one example, or leave people out.
cards.explanation: Variety, checked labels and realistic examples make data **better**. Wrong or rushed labels teach wrong lessons, copies add nothing new, and one office leaves everyone else out.

cards.prompt: One example has the wrong label.
cards.hint: Read each example's name and its label. Do they match?
cards.nudge: Look for an example whose label doesn't match what it is.
cards.explanation: "Long banana" was labelled **Apple**, and it sat closest to the ripe banana. Leaving it out fixes it: one wrong label can cause a mistake.

cards.prompt: A spam filter learned only from **English** and misses **Spanish** spam. Which **one** addition helps most?

options.nudge: That's lots more data, but does any of it show Spanish spam?

options.text: 200 labelled Spanish messages, spam and normal
200 Spanish spam messages, all labelled spam
options.nudge: Close! But if every Spanish message is spam, what will it think of a friend?

options.text: The same English messages again, twice over
options.nudge: Copies add nothing new. What's missing from its examples?

cards.hint: What's missing from its examples, and what happens to normal Spanish messages?
cards.explanation: It needs **Spanish examples** of **both kinds**: spam only would teach it that Spanish means spam, so friends get flagged. More English adds nothing about Spanish.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- A model learns only from its **training data**, gaps and all.
- One word, or one example, can tip it the wrong way.
- Better data beats more data: checked, varied and realistic.

Next: how to tell if a model is any good.
